bullet_fields: TWO fields, because there are two different relationships and collapsing them double-counts a bullet. `bullets` is the canon project's OWN bullets -- the set an example project is responsible for backing; across the 11 canon paths it partitions all 49 exactly once. `backs_bullets` is what an ALREADY-EXISTING artifact is cited as backing. example-beta:P5-B3 is the case that forced the split: it is a bullet of example-beta P5 (beta-artifact-5) AND its backing field names Research/example-cache-benchmark. Both are true, so one `bullets` field would have claimed it twice and made the 49-bullet partition read as 50.

derived_from.note: Every canon, project and bullet id in this file was DERIVED from the committed canon snapshot, never transcribed. a design rule's 'derived by filtering, never typed' applies to the ids as much as to the counts.

gpu_required_basis: Read from the per-path Technology Stack in the project technology-stack document, not measured on the filesystem. alpha-artifact-4 serves a model on the RTX 4050; alpha-artifact-5 runs sentence-transformers embeddings and a QLoRA leg; beta-artifact-1 loads bge-m3 and bge-reranker-v2-m3. The other eleven need no GPU. This is a READING of a documented stack and is marked as such rather than presented as a measurement.

naming.note: G2's resolution travels WITH the expected set rather than living only in a plan. results/figures.json carries the numbers; this file carries the expected set; the banned spelling above is refused outright by the banned-spelling rule, and conformance.py FAILS on its existence in any artifact.

scan_root.note: Declared as a RULE relative to the repository root, never as an absolute path: a tracked file must not bake in a home directory, and the same rule must resolve correctly in every checkout. tools/tests/conftest.py declared the identical value; the two are one assertion with two ends, and a disagreement between them is the finding rather than a value to pick between. Enumeration stops at depth 1 -- that depth is the whole mechanism by which a design rule holds, because fixtures/broken-artifacts/ IS contained in the scan root and is never ENUMERATED by it.

slugs.no_row_reason: Program factoring, not a canon example project: it backs no canon bullet. The slug returns zero bullet-scoped hits in BOTH canons and has no build_paths entry in either.

Cited by no bullet in either canon. Verified with a BULLET-SCOPED probe: the document-scoped scan of example-beta returns 1 hit, at $.consistency_notes[13], whose text says this artifact is 'cited nowhere here' -- the canon affirming the exclusion, not contradicting it.

status_field: a design rule extension ratified by the owner as the status rule. Values are built | pending. A pending slug whose directory EXISTS is a FINDING (the manifest is stale). A built slug whose directory is MISSING is a FAIL. pending reaching 0 is a project requirement's closeout criterion. status is owner/plan-set-set and is NEVER written by a build agent -- the same posture as a design rule's waivers.
